Key Findings
Hong Kong Qualitative Evaluation · 2025 highlights
01
2025 was a moderately active year in Hong Kong, with notable local reviews: Nestle to Spark Foundry, AS Watson to Hearts & Science, OSIM to UM, alongside a high volume of retentions including Vitasoy, HK Disneyland, KAO and ASAHI. Regional and global mandates play a secondary role: most strategic decisions are made elsewhere, with Hong Kong largely receiving the outcome.
02
The volume of retentions partly explains the stability at the top, where Starcom leads for a second consecutive year. The biggest movement is downward: Carat falls four places to 6th, weighed down by the loss of AS Watson, while Havas slips two ranks. Conversely, PHD and OMD both gain ground.
03
The OMG-IPG merger makes Omnicom Media the new benchmark in Hong Kong. Combining OMD, PHD and the newly ranked Hearts & Science, the group leads in pitch volume and wins. Alongside Publicis Media, both groups stand clearly ahead of the rest, consistent with the global picture that emerged from the merger.
04
WPP Media faces the most difficult year, posting a negative new business balance driven by a high number of departures. Mindshare and Wavemaker have yet to find their footing after several years of transition, a pattern observed across several Asian markets.
05

Group client portfolios reveal distinct profiles:

  • Publicis leads the new business balance alongside Omnicom Media, but its portfolio relies heavily on international accounts won through global pitches, leaving the group with a more limited local presence than its score would suggest.
  • Omnicom Media now offers the most balanced profile.
  • Havas stands out for its local depth and diversified book.
  • WPP Media continues to show a structural imbalance between wins and departures, increasingly reflected in its quali-score trajectory.

Key Findings
Perimeter and executive summary from the original OAV report
01

Perimeter

The perimeter studied by RECMA includes the six international media groups. The total market studied is estimated by RECMA to be $2,417m in Overall Activity Volume.
02

Market trend

After a soar in 2023, RECMA estimates an increase of the Hong Kong market in 2024 (+10%). Over three years, the increase is 43%.
03

Non-traditional activity

Traditional media is about $805m and the average share of non-traditional activity is increasing by : 67% in 2024 from 64% in 2023.
04

Top 5 agencies in 2024

For 2024, OMD leads ahead of Starcom. PHD and Zenith rank #3, followed by Carat. The Top 5 agencies represent 59% of the total market studied.
05

Group ranking in 2024

Excluding independent agencies, OMG is leading with 25.8% industry share ahead of Publicis Media at 24.5%.

Technical Remarks
Agency-by-agency explanations from the OAV full report
Select an agency

OMD

+20%

OMD saw strong performance in 2024, supported by new business wins like Maxim's and increased investment in digital (+6pts). While traditional media spend decreased for Beiersdorf and Octopus, this was offset by growth from clients such as HKTDC, Vita Green, and McDonald’s. The departure of Estée Lauder had limited impact.

Starcom incl. Spark

+31%

Starcom maintained strong momentum in 2024, thanks to major client wins such as FrieslandCampina and Pacific Century, sustained growth for P&G, and full-year impact of accounts gained in 2023.

PHD

+10%

PHD continued to grow in 2024, supported by new business wins including Trip.com, Vitasoy and Mox, plus accounts gained in 2023 such as Tanjai and WeChat Pay.

Zenith

+13%

Zenith sustained its positive momentum in 2024, building on the full-year impact of AIA and continued growth from clients such as Walt Disney and Deliveroo.

Carat

+9%

Carat maintained its growth trajectory in 2024, supported by new client additions such as Swatch and Swire, plus several wins from 2023.

dentsu X

+5%

dentsu X maintained steady growth in 2024, supported by Prada and Wai Yuen Tong, while building on 2023 momentum.

EssenceMediacom

+5%

EssenceMediacom sustained positive momentum with Hang Seng Bank and Zero Finance wins, plus increased investment from Uber and Mars.

Mindshare

-9%

Mindshare declined in 2024, impacted by the full-year effect of past losses and additional departures such as Foodpanda and Suntory.

Wavemaker

-7%

Wavemaker faced a more challenging 2024, impacted by key departures such as BBK Electronics, Swatch and Friesland.

Havas Media

+20%

Havas maintained positive momentum in 2024, supported by new wins such as Inchcape, Emma Sleep and Venetian Cotai, plus HK Jockey Club expansion.

UM incl. Initiative

-10%

Mediabrands posted a slight decline in 2024. New business wins did not fully offset upcoming departures like Amazon, Lego and Kenvue.

iProspect

+11%

iProspect sustained growth, building on recent client wins such as Pizza Hut, PHD and KFC.

Key Findings · Global Research 2026
Summary of major trends across all tracked markets
📈
Growth Acceleration
Overall media agency activity volume grew by an average of +14% across tracked markets, led by APAC (+19%) and the Americas (+12%).
🏆
Network Consolidation
Top 3 networks (Publicis, Omnicom, dentsu) now account for 58% of total tracked billings, up from 52% in 2024.
🌏
APAC Leadership
APAC markets continue to outperform global averages both in qualitative scores and new business activity, with 6 of the top 10 ranked agencies based in the region.
🔄
New Business Momentum
Global new business activity reached record levels in 2025, with pitches increasing by +22% year-on-year. Havas networks showed the strongest positive balance in APAC.

01
Industry growth
The media agency industry grew by 6.2% in 2024, compared with +5.8% in 2023, across RECMA's perimeter of six international media groups, standalones and major independents.
02
OMD remains the largest network worldwide
OMD maintains the top position ahead of EssenceMediacom and Mindshare, with a significantly higher growth rate (+9.5%) than direct competitors.
03
WPP Media still leads by group
WPP Media remains the largest group by volume (23.5%), while Publicis Media is closing the gap (+9.4% growth) and the potential OMG + IPG perimeter would become dominant at 30.6%.
04
New business impact remains selective
Spark Foundry and OMG agencies benefit strongly from recent wins (Kimberly Clark, Lowe's, Amazon Americas), while EssenceMediacom is significantly affected by major global departures.
05
2025 forecast — Publicis to benefit most
Publicis Media is expected to benefit from recent major wins including Mars, Paramount, Santander, Coca-Cola USA, Unilever SEA, MediaMarkt, Sky EMEA and Hershey USA. Initiative will be negatively impacted by the departure of Amazon.
